paragraphs: BusWhere sells real-time bus tracking to schools and districts, so staff can watch buses on a map and spend less time answering phone calls from parents asking where the bus is. Parents get a notification on their phone when the bus is getting close and can watch it move toward the stop. The same tracking is sold for shuttle fleets at corporate headquarters, hospitals, rental car companies, hotels and airports.

Routes are set up in minutes with drag and drop route creation. Setup handles drop-a-pin stops, off-road stops in parking lots, circular routes and multiple buses on one route. Vehicle data covers fuel levels, odometer and sudden braking. The resulting logs are interactive and downloadable. Operators can also bring existing hardware, since the product integrates with Geotab, Samsara, Zonar and others.

Administrators using the product are said to report a drop in calls asking when the bus will arrive, along with higher rider satisfaction. For bus companies, the process is to plug the tracker in on the bus, register online and start tracking. Schools are told they can be running in under an hour. The site lists an address in North Bethesda, Maryland. It also cites a United States patent.
